title: X5 RetailHero heterogeneity generalization test (mirrors Hillstrom forecaster_powered.py)
objective: Test whether the simulator's certified Hillstrom 'who-responds-more' heterogeneity-ranking capability (blinded Sonnet expert-forecaster, Spearman rho +0.42) GENERALIZES to a second independent real RCT: the X5 RetailHero uplift dataset.
treatment: retailer SMS promotion (treatment_flg=1) vs no-SMS holdout (=0)
segment_definition: gender(F/M) x age-bucket(under35 / 35to54 / 55plus) x tenure-bucket(first_issue year: 2017=long, 2018=mid, 2019=new). Gender 'U' (unknown) dropped (no interpretable audience description). Ages <14 or >90 dropped. Floor n>=200 per arm.

method.framing: expert in retail SMS-promotion causal effects; predicts the treatment-vs-holdout change for each audience described from covariates ONLY (real uplift NEVER shown)
method.output: numeric predicted responsiveness (predicted uplift in percentage points) per segment
method.blinding: audience descriptions built from gender/age/tenure covariates only; no uplift, no target rates, no ranking leaked

scoring.primary: Spearman rank-rho between predicted scores and REAL per-segment uplift (using repo spearman_rho, same as Hillstrom)
scoring.significance: label-permutation p-value on |rho|, 5000 shuffles, seed=42 (mirrors forecaster_powered.py perm_p)

registered_prediction: We EXPECT generalization (rho > 0.30, p < 0.05). The X5 SMS promotion belongs to the same marketing-nudge family as the Hillstrom email campaign, and the covariates (age/gender/tenure) carry real, forecastable demand signal. We register moderate confidence: a single-model, 18-segment test on a different retailer/market (Russian grocery loyalty) may attenuate rho below the Hillstrom +0.42 even if the capability transfers.
stopping_rule: Run all 18 segments once at temperature 0.0; no peeking, no segment re-selection after seeing predictions. Result is whatever the single pre-registered run produces.
